reconstruction: For every real m-by-n matrix A, this literal constructor returns R:m-by-min(m,n) and Q:min(m,n)-by-n, proving A=RQ and QQ^T=I. If m<=n it eliminates A^T using signed half-angle adjacent row planes from the changing matrix and extracts the leading residual rows transposed and leading accumulated-transform rows. If m>n it returns exactly A and I_n. Rank deficiency and empty dimensions need no additional premise. The construction fixes a mathematical rule on exact reals, not an executable finite-bit preprocessing pipeline.

declaration_comparison.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.ConstructiveThinLQ.Factorization
declaration_comparison.checked_type: {m n : Nat} -> Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) Real -> Nat -> Type
declaration_comparison.comparison: Generic record at parameter r, containing R:m-by-r, Q:r-by-n and proofs A=R*Q, Q*Q.transpose=I_r. Lesson correctly distinguishes the record from its producer. The record is not claimed inhabited at every r and has no triangular/rank/positive/unique/cost field. Actual factor chooses r=min(m,n).

declaration_comparison.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.ConstructiveThinLQ.wideR
declaration_comparison.checked_type: {m n : Nat} -> m<=n -> Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) Real -> Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) Real
declaration_comparison.comparison: Literal body reduced A.transpose (Fin.castLE hmn k) i matches R_ik=T(A^T)_ki. The first index is the residual row-prefix index, and the second is the original data-row index; there is no existence-witness replacement.

declaration_comparison.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.ConstructiveThinLQ.wideQ
declaration_comparison.checked_type: {m n : Nat} -> m<=n -> Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) Real -> Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) Real
declaration_comparison.comparison: Literal body transform A.transpose (Fin.castLE hmn k) j matches Q_kj=S(A^T)_kj. Both factors use the same specified procedure, although the functional definitions do not promise shared cached evaluation.

declaration_comparison.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.ConstructiveThinLQ.wide_factorization
declaration_comparison.checked_type: forall {m n} (hmn:m<=n) (A:Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) Real), A=wideR hmn A*wideQ hmn A
declaration_comparison.comparison: Transposes actual provider recovery, then uses reduced_zero_below and ThinLQ.sum_prefix_of_zero to discard exactly the residual tail ell>=m. This is the lesson's entrywise proof, with no full-rank or caller-supplied recovery premise.

declaration_comparison.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.ConstructiveThinLQ.wide_orthogonal
declaration_comparison.checked_type: forall {m n} (hmn:m<=n) (A:Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) Real), wideQ hmn A*(wideQ hmn A).transpose=1
declaration_comparison.comparison: Uses mul_eq_one_comm on the square transform's S^T S=I and reads SS^T entries at the prefix embeddings. This proves row orthogonality QQ^T, not the generally false Q^T Q=I_n when m<n.

declaration_comparison.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.ConstructiveThinLQ.factorOfLE
declaration_comparison.checked_type: {m n} -> m<=n -> (A:Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) Real) -> Factorization A m
declaration_comparison.comparison: Packages exactly wideR and wideQ with the two internally proved equations. A and the shape guard are the inputs, not a factorization/orthogonality certificate supplied by the caller.

declaration_comparison.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.ConstructiveThinLQ.factor
declaration_comparison.checked_type: {m n} -> (A:Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) Real) -> Factorization A (min m n)
declaration_comparison.comparison: by_cases m<=n chooses wide at equality; otherwise literal record <A,1,...>. Equality transports change only the dependent dimension. No Classical.choose of ThinLQ.exists_thin_lq or gramSchmidt factor selection occurs in this constructor.

declaration_comparison.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.ConstructiveThinLQ.factor_correct
declaration_comparison.checked_type: forall {m n} (A:Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) Real), A=(factor A).R*(factor A).Q and (factor A).Q*(factor A).Q.transpose=1
declaration_comparison.comparison: Projects both proofs from this same actual returned record. It is a packaging consequence, not an independent algorithm; the substantive construction/correctness is in literal factor/wide providers and their proofs. The lesson does not mistake this wrapper for finite-bit or quantum closure.

provider_and_topology_comparison.signed_rule: pairNorm is sqrt(x^2+y^2). splitAngle is rational zero at pairNorm=0 and otherwise ExactAngle.real(2*alpha) with the negative arccos branch exactly when y<0. ExactAngle.eval interprets .real literally; eliminationAngle negates splitAngle.eval, hence theta=-2alpha exactly. AdjacentGivens.eliminate_pair proves the ordered pivot goes to (pairNorm,0). This matches both source-first sign discriminators, including x<0,y=0 and negative y.
provider_and_topology_comparison.row_plane: rotateRows mixes complete ordered rows with cos(theta/2), -sin(theta/2); sin(theta/2), cos(theta/2), fixing all other rows. Step adjacency supplies distinctness. The zero-pair theorem proves an actual identity full-row update, not a default matrix or division-zero escape.
provider_and_topology_comparison.changing_matrix: columnSweepSteps emits the current bottom pair's eliminationAngle and recurses on eliminateEntry A first second col. Rectangular sweepSteps concatenates that current-column list before a tail computed on columnSweep A. Thus both scalar angles and later columns depend on the updated matrix, not the original matrix or an externally supplied log.
provider_and_topology_comparison.chronology: applySteps executes head first; stepsMatrix(step::rest)=stepsMatrix(rest)*step.matrix. The action theorem identifies this literal product with the residual. The source S=G_s...G_1 is the same convention.
provider_and_topology_comparison.zeros: RectangularGivens.UpperPrefix expresses zeros below already processed columns. columnSweep_upperPrefix and sweep_upperPrefix prove propagation and reduced_zero_below for arbitrary rectangular A, independently of rank or orthogonality of A.
provider_and_topology_comparison.orthogonality_recovery: stepsMatrix_orthogonal proves S^T S=I using actual plane orthogonality. transform_mul proves SB=T; exact_recovery proves S^T T=B. Square left/right inverse equivalence then provides row orthogonality in the target proof.
provider_and_topology_comparison.prefix_removal: ThinLQ is completely inspected: its existence result uses Gram-Schmidt completion, but ConstructiveThinLQ references only sum_prefix_of_zero. Importing ThinLQ does not mean its existence witness selected these factors.
provider_and_topology_comparison.case_topology: The target combines two equations within each guarded dimension branch. The wide and tall branches are exhaustive alternatives, not two independently sufficient unguarded routes for every shape. Existing SO decomposition requirements in AdjacentGivens are not imported as hypotheses of rectangular elimination or the target factor theorem.
provider_and_topology_comparison.graph_limit: These are inspected source/proof-call relationships, not an exported elaborated proof-term graph or a categorical certification.

target.reason: Actual all-shape real matrix reconstruction A=RQ at r=min(m,n), not rank(A), with literal factors prescribed by the source.

normalization.reason: Only Q rows are normalized/orthogonal: QQ^T=I_r. Arbitrary A is not normalized, and no prepared-state normalization is implied.

registers.reason: Numerical Fin row/column indices are not qubit registers; no endian, tensor factor, Gray-code or wire mapping is asserted by this target.

oracles.reason: A is an arbitrary matrix function; no costed entry oracle, coherent query interface or constant-time lookup assumption is certified.

ancillas_phases.reason: No quantum ancilla/garbage or global/relative phase claim. Signed real entries and ordered plane signs are literal equalities, not equality modulo phase; their preservation was checked separately.

error_success.reason: The matrix equations are exact. There is no epsilon, norm-distance, probability, postselection branch or numerical error certificate.

resources.reason: The lesson asserts no total arithmetic/runtime or quantum-resource bound. Provider rotation-list length <=N*M is not operand-bit, matrix-entry evaluation, storage/copying, finite-bit or circuit cost.

rank_sign_shape_empty_audit.square: same: equality enters wide. A 1-by-1 negative scalar is retained in R because no pair is swept; no positive final diagonal premise or conclusion is present.

rank_sign_shape_empty_audit.empty: same: m=0 uses wide with empty residual/prefix and no columns; n=0<m uses tall I_0; m=n=0 uses wide. No positive dimension is required and no empty identity is replaced by scalar 1.
rank_sign_shape_empty_audit.zero_pair_zero_matrix: same: actual zero-angle identity steps remain in the log; with A=0 all are identities, leading to the fixed identity row prefix rather than arbitrary completion.
